Two things, kept separate on purpose

Balance goes down. The Vault fills up. Money only ever moves one way — unless a Pass fails to validate, in which case it comes straight back.

Every Pass shows its terms, its expiry, and its state. Present from here at the counter; it is validated live and consumed once. Cards draw down instead.

Why not one wallet? A vault is a place things stay. A balance is something you spend down. Keeping them apart keeps the mental model honest for the customer, and keeps the stored-value component clearly identified for the people who regulate it.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Mezzofy Vault?

A consumer app (iOS, Android, Web, and NFC card) that securely stores, organizes, and redeems your Passes.

What is the difference between a Vault and a wallet balance?

A wallet holds money; the Vault holds Passes — each a specific, single-use tokenized offer, redeemed by tapping, scanning, or presenting.

Does the Vault work with Apple Wallet and Google Pay?

Yes. Passes can be added to Apple Wallet and Google Pay, alongside the Vault app and an NFC physical card.

How do I redeem a Pass from the Vault?

Open the Pass and tap NFC, scan the QR or barcode, or present the code at the counter — it is consumed once on validation.
